newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume jumps on arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume jumps on arbitrage.

text.p: Traded volume on the Istanbul gold exchange leapt to 2,330 kilos on Friday, the second highest volume ever and up sharply from Thursday's 1,370 kilos on banks' heavy arbitrage transactions, dealers said.
Gold closed higher at $351.00 an ounce and 1,433,400 lira per gram from $348.60 and 1,424,000 lira on Thursday, in line with the far eastern markets.
"There was strong arbitrage activity among banks because of the fluctuations in the lira/dollar rate and tiny real demand from the free market," said one dealer.
The market's daily record volume was 2,570 kilos seen on January 8.
The Turkish lira closed easier at 126,925 against the dollar versus Thursday's close of 126,830 in line with the dollar/mark parity after it firmed to 126,800 earlier in the day.
Of the day's trade, 58 percent was conducted in dollar terms.
